title: Jack Hid A Secret TV In A Potato Chip Bag While L Watched With 64 Cameras . . . (Episode 8)
caption:
In Death Note episode 8, L hides 64 cameras in Jack's house, and Jack still kills two criminals on the news while eating potato chips.
The trick is a tiny TV inside the chip bag. Follow for episode 9!

#deathnote #anime #animerecap #animeexplained #fyp
comment: Would you have caught Jack's chip bag trick, or fallen for it like L? Why?

segments.say: Jack eats potato chips in front of 64 hidden cameras, and two *criminals* die.
To see how it got here, go back to the day L decides to put cameras in Jack's *house*.
L is watching security footage of the day FBI agent Ray Penber *died*.
He spots something odd. Ray carried an envelope in, but it was gone when he *collapsed*.
So L asks the room one question. What if Kira was standing on that *train*?
Everyone else says no way, because Kira can kill from far *away*.
Meanwhile, Jack has spent four days writing criminals' names in the Death Note, weeks in *advance*.
Ryuk asks what he is trying to *prove*.
Jack calls it insurance. If he ends up in a cell and criminals stop dying, everyone will know. Cold, but *smart*.
Back with L, a call comes in, and he learns the name of Ray's fiancee, *Naomi Misora*.
She vanished the day after he died, and L thinks Kira got to her *first*.
So L narrows it down to the two men Ray was tailing, Jack's father and Deputy Director *Kitamura*.
Then L drops the bomb. He wants wiretaps and cameras in *both* houses.
At home, Jack wipes his computer and hides his Death Note clippings, just in *case*.
The task force is furious. If this leaks, it is a civil rights *scandal*.
L shrugs. Even a one percent chance is too much to *ignore*.
Jack's own father agrees, even if it means cameras in his own *bathroom*.
L does not do things by *halves*.
Watari gets to work, and by the next day the cameras are in, waiting for *Jack*.
Jack gets home to an empty house, and every step he takes is already on *camera*.
He climbs the stairs and checks the trap on his bedroom *door*.
In L's room, Jack's father watches his son lock himself away, and he looks *worried*.
Jack drags Ryuk outside, where no camera can *see* them.
He tells Ryuk there are probably cameras and wiretaps hidden all over his *house*.
Jack set three traps: a paper in the door, a low handle, and a pencil lead on the *hinge*.
The pencil lead is broken. Someone has been in his *room*.
Jack did not like that at *all*.
Then he walks into a bookstore and buys a book about wiretaps and surveillance. Fighting fire with *fire*.
A floating apple would look like a magic trick on camera, so Ryuk has to quit *apples*.
Ryuk says apples are his cigarettes. Without them, he does *handstands*.
Jack has a deal. Find every camera in the house, and maybe you get a blind spot to eat *apples*.
Ryuk loves it. A camera hunt sounds like *fun*.
Jack, meanwhile, leaves a few magazines lying around, the kind a teen would hide from his *parents*.
In L's room, Jack's father sighs. It is normal for a teen, but a little too *obvious*.
L says that is exactly what Jack wants them to *think*.
Back in his room, Ryuk finds the first camera, hidden in the air *conditioner*.
Jack figures it out fast. L has narrowed his list, and Jack is on it. Smart *kid*.
Luckily, he had planned for this very *day*.
L has Watari ask the broadcasters to play a message, just as the family sits down to *dinner*.
The news says Interpol is sending fifteen hundred investigators to *Japan*.
Jack does not buy it. He knows it is a trick to shake *him*.
He calls the whole thing desperate, and says Kira would see right *through* it.
L watches the screen in silence, and his best test just *failed*.
Later, Jack grabs a bag of potato chips as a late night *snack*.
Upstairs, Ryuk collapses on the floor. He has found every camera in the *room*.
Ryuk counted sixty four of them. L was not taking any *chances*.
Jack smiles. He has lined up three more weeks of deaths *already*.
But to stay clear, he must look like he has no idea what is on the *news*.
So Jack hides a tiny TV inside his chip bag. Disgustingly *clever*.
With one hand he does math. With the other, he writes the names the news just *said*.
Then he eats a chip, and forty seconds later a criminal *drops*.
Jack stretches, crumples the bag, and tosses the evidence in the *trash*.
Downstairs, Watari reads the news. A bank clerk and a purse snatcher just died of heart *attacks*.
But Jack has studied at his desk the whole *night*.
So anyone who never saw the news cannot be Kira, and that clears Jack's *family*.
Even L admits the Yagami house looks almost too *innocent*.
Morning comes, and Jack's mom reminds him it is garbage *day*.
The truck rolls up, and the little TV goes into the *crusher*.
Jack watches from his window with a smirk. L has 64 cameras and not one shred of *proof*.
But L has one more move, and it ends face to *face*. Follow for episode 9!
